question: What resource limits can cause a Soroban transaction to fail, like CPU instructions, memory, and ledger entries?

golden.answer: Soroban meters several independent resources: transaction size, footprint entry counts and bytes, disk reads and writes, CPU instructions, memory, ledger-entry size, event bytes and return-value size. The limits are validator-voted network settings that change, so inspect the target network instead of quoting numbers. Declared maxima can fail at validation or simulation; actual CPU, memory, I/O and event use fails at apply time. Most have ledger-wide budgets, but memory is capped per transaction only.
keyFacts: Limits span tx size, footprint, I/O, CPU, memory, entry size, event and return bytes.
Limits are validator-voted settings that change; values should not be frozen.
Declared maxima fail at validation; actual CPU, memory, I/O, event use fails at apply.
Many limits have ledger-wide budgets, but memory is capped per transaction only.
avoid: Do NOT reduce limits to one gas scalar or freeze network numbers.
Do NOT say every limit fails only during execution.
golden.notes: Naming `readBytes` or `refundableFee` as current XDR field names is stale; labelling them older XDR is correct.

corroboration.claim: Soroban resource enforcement is phased: declared size/footprint constraints can fail validation/preflight, actual execution resources fail at apply, and many but not all transaction limits have ledger aggregates.
